items.title: Anthropic's Drug Deal: One-Person Company as Proof of Concept
points: Anthropic acquired Mithril Medicine, a one-person biotech startup founded by Cody Tranbarger (Harvard MBA, Goldman Sachs background), which used Claude AI to coordinate 11 external labs and compress muscular dystrophy drug development from a typical four-to-seven years into 18 months.
The company targets clinical-trial readiness by end of 2028, claiming AI assisted across the entire discovery pipeline (chemistry, biology, project coordination) rather than one bottleneck.

Critics (Scorpion Capital, Lenny Rachitsky) question whether founder credentials and support load make massive-scale one-person companies realistic; supporters cite it as vindication of Sam Altman's prediction that solo founders plus AI can build billion-dollar enterprises.
The deal signals labs shifting from selling AI tokens (API usage) to owning outcomes, betting drug discovery becomes a defensible revenue stream distinct from commodity AI APIs.

items.title: Google's Genie 4: Real-Time Interactive World Simulation
points: Genie 4 combines Gemini Omni (multimodal large language model), Gemini 3.8 Flash (a fast reasoning model), and Google's audio models to generate fully playable 3D worlds steerable in real time via text prompts, with sharply improved physics and human realism over Genie 3.

New features include real-time camera, weather, object, and character steering; native audio (music, effects, speech, though dialogue remains hollow); and an in-the-loop agent (Gemini 3.8 Flash) that breaks tasks into steps and verifies causality for reliability.

For robotics, Gemini 4 Argon decomposes robot tasks into live captions fed into Genie 4, letting robots train in simulated environments and replan mid-task without costly physical-world trial-and-error.
Still capped at two-minute simulations and in demo form, but nearing practical use for training AI agents, game development, and simulation pipelines.

items.title: OpenAI's Science Disclosure Dilemma
points: OpenAI appointed expert review groups after criticism of earlier unvetted math-proof releases, but kept a claimed Yang-Mills existence proof (a major unsolved problem in mathematical physics) private for expert review, triggering backlash.
OpenAI's own mathematics advisory board and outside researchers argue verification should happen in public; physics experts counter they want certainty of correctness before release to avoid chaos.
The dispute highlights broader unease about AI labs controlling which scientific results go public and when, regardless of disclosure strategy chosen.

items.title: Anthropic IPO Revives AI Trade Amid Market Skepticism
points: Anthropic's S-1 filing (a registration statement required before a US IPO) revealed $112+ billion in cash before IPO proceeds during a tech drawdown and four-month semiconductor bear market; Nasdaq rose 2% and the Philadelphia Semiconductor Index rebounded about 6% on renewed confidence in AI capex paths to profitability.

A potential $100 billion raise would signal capital access for the entire AI sector, per the Wall Street Journal; investor focus shifted from AI-risk concerns ("p(doom)") to upside potential ("p(boom)").
The S-1 names Google and OpenAI as major competitors, positioning Anthropic as a pure-play AI company distinct from cloud vendors.

items.title: DeepMind Sells TPU Chips to Rivals
points: Google DeepMind now sells its TPU (Tensor Processing Unit, custom AI accelerator chip) hardware to OpenAI and Oracle, positioning Google to compete via hardware distribution in addition to AI model capability.
Google also released new Gemini base models (Argon and Carbon) enabling faster post-training iteration (the process of refining a trained model with additional tuning).
